thread:
kevin: quick brain dump — thinking we should separate lease/eviction telemetry from the dataplane control channel. right now the lease heartbeat + observability emits ~N metrics per tenant which spikes during migration/failover and clogs the controlplane. idea: move to a dedicated streaming sink with sampled deltas and a compact lease-state summary for the control path. low-risk prototype this week?

maddie: +1. the controlplane queueing latencies are visible in canaries. during a simulated region fail we saw 3–4x enlistment messages. the metric cardinality is the killer.

amira: curious — are you proposing a full rewrite of the lease protocol or just the telemetry channel? my concern is coupling: if we change export format we need backward compatibility with old operators.

kevin: not a protocol rewrite. keep the lease ownership RPCs as-is. split observability: a consumer-facing summarized lease-state (owner, expiry, hint) that is cheap and canonical, and an async high-cardinality stream we can shard and TTL aggressively. control RPCs still authoritative.

srinivas: how would that affect failover detection? we rely on frequent heartbeats for fast failover in active/active. if we sample the stream we might add blind spots.

kevin: good point. plan is: heartbeats remain local and frequent between regional agents; the global controlplane relies on summarized lease-state (compact + last-write vector). sampling applies only to verbose metrics (histograms, per-tenant debug traces). for SLO-critical flags we keep full fidelity. cheap summary example: `{owner: region-a, seq: 3921, ttl_s: 12, topology_hint: eu-west}`

runtime-bot: deploy-check: can we run the summarizer as sidecar with local memory-only cache? that would avoid an extra network hop during steady-state.

maddie: sidecar seems fine. ops note: need to ensure sidecar crash doesn't cause lease churn. maybe have the region-agent continue emitting minimal heartbeat until summarizer reconnects.

amira: on the storage side, I propose adding a small k/v lease-index table that stores only the compact summary. reads are cheap and we can garbage collect by seq. avoids costly tombstone scans in global DB.

kevin: exactly. keeps the heavy traces in a time-series store with aggressive retention. the k/v index is the single source for controlplane decisions. time-series for postmortem and anomaly detection only.

srinivas: we'll need instrumentation to validate that the summary doesn't diverge from authoritative state. suggest a shadow-check mode where summaries include a short HMAC of the authoritative lease payload so we can detect corruption without full payload round-trip.

amira: HMAC sounds reasonable. also let's codify versioning for the summary schema so we can roll changes without rolling the whole fleet.

ops-bot: note added to runbook: "if summarizer sidecar fails, region-agent sets lease-summary: degraded and continues controlplane heartbeats"

kevin: next steps: (1) prototype sidecar summarizer that subscribes to local heartbeat topic and writes compact summaries to k/v index, (2) add shadow HMAC check, (3) chaos test for summarizer crash and region failover, (4) telemetry dashboard showing cardinality reduction. volunteering: I can hack the prototype. need help from infra for k/v shard and srinivas for HMAC bits.

maddie: I can take chaos tests + canary. amira can you own the DB index schema?

amira: yep. will sketch schema and a migration plan — want to avoid a global rolling migration.

srinivas: I can do the HMAC and tests. question: what TTL semantics on the compact entry? we need a small grace window for clock skew.

kevin: propose TTL = 3x expected heartbeat interval + 2s fudge. we'll calibrate in canary.

maddie: sounds good. can we add a short doc in arch repo with diagrams? a single pic showing sidecar -> kv-index -> controlplane, and the time-series sink for verbose traces.

kevin: will do. I'll open an RFC follow-up with design + sequence diagram and mark it RFC: low-risk. can we sync tomorrow 11am for 20m?

amira: ✅

srinivas: ✅

maddie: ✅
